To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the probability distribution of future effects on the environment from an activity is more uncertain when that activity is novel than when it is familiar, (2) the probability distribution is less uncertain when the activity is familiar and the environmental effects are well understood, and (3) the probability distribution can be made more uncertain by introducing uncertainty into the environmental effects of the activity.

the probability of an activity having a future effect that is greater than the present value of the activity's costs is greater when the costs of the activity are covered by a bond than when the costs are covered by a loan.

the incentive to research in activities involving uncertain future effects is greater the more the effects of the activity are expected to be adverse and the more difficult it is to predict the effects of the activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a class of problems in which the future effects of activities are uncertain, and in which the only source of infonnation about those effects is the research undertaken to investigate them.
a class of activities which have no historical precedents and for which there exist, therefore, no historical data from which to infer the future effects of the activity.
the following question: What are the implications of uncertainty concerning the effects of present activities on the incentive to undertake research into those activities?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, other things being equal, the greater the uncertainty of the future outcomes of a given activity, the greater the need to research that activity in advance of its introduction.
there is no conclusive statement to be made on the basis of the available evidence.
the more research is done, the more likely it is that the future effects will be correctly identified and that the more accurate the probability distribution of the future effects will become.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
environmental bonds can be used to provide a powerful incentive for research in activities involving uncertain future effects, including Shackle-crucual activities.
the environmental bond is an efficient means of financing environmental research, and that it can be used to induce a firm's managers to undertake such research.
the environmental bonds are an effective tool for reducing the risk associated with the introduction of new products and technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incentive to conduct such research is greater in the presence of a liability bond than in the absence of one.
the incentive to undertake this research is likely to be less the greater the uncertainty of the effects of the activity in question.

, in the absence of historical data, the incentive to research in activities involving uncertain future effects is greater the more severe the environmental bonds that must be paid to undertake those activities.
